issues.legal_issue: A local board’s authority to regulate markets does not extend to prohibiting private persons from operating a market.
material_facts: The board made a bye-law prohibiting anyone from establishing, maintaining, or running a cattle market within its jurisdiction.
The board’s statutory bye-law power was directed to promoting or maintaining inhabitants’ health, safety, and convenience, and included power to regulate markets.
The petitioner operated a cattle market on privately held land.
issues.conclusion: The prohibitory bye-law exceeded the board’s authority and was ultra vires.
issues.legal_principle: Section 174(1) of the United Provinces District Board Act, 1922, confined bye-laws to the stated public-welfare purposes, while Section 174(2)(l) authorized regulation of markets. A power to regulate markets did not authorize a bye-law prohibiting them.

predicates.bylaw_challenge_proceeding: A person challenges a local board’s bye-law in a proceeding seeking judicial review.
predicates.board_power_limited_to_public_welfare_re: The board’s authority to make bye-laws is limited to public-welfare purposes and includes authority to regulate markets.
predicates.bylaw_prohibits_market_operation: The bye-law bars people from establishing or operating the relevant kind of market, rather than regulating how it operates.

issues.definition: When a challenged bye-law-making power is limited to public-welfare regulation and the bye-law instead prohibits market operation, the bye-law is beyond the board’s authority.

issues.legal_issue: A local board’s blanket prohibition on operating a market unlawfully interferes with the right to carry on a business.
material_facts: The petitioner operated a cattle market for sales and charged commission.
The bye-law prohibited anyone from establishing, maintaining, or running a cattle market within the board’s jurisdiction.
The board served a notice under the bye-law directing the petitioner not to hold the market.
issues.conclusion: The bye-law violated the petitioner’s right to carry on business and was void; the order made under it was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Article 19(1)(g) protects the right to carry on a business. The Court relied on Rashid Ahmed v. Municipal Board, Kairana, 1950 AIR(SC) 163, which held that an absolute prohibition on business, where no licence could be obtained and a monopoly had been created, imposed an unreasonable restriction. Here, the bye-law prohibited the petitioner from carrying on the market business.

predicates.business_restriction_challenge_proceedin: A person challenges a restriction on carrying on a business in a judicial proceeding.
predicates.person_operates_market_for_business: A person operates a market as a commercial activity.
predicates.bylaw_bars_all_market_operation: A bye-law prohibits all operation of the relevant kind of market within the board’s jurisdiction.

issues.definition: When a person challenges a business restriction, operates a market commercially, and the bye-law bars all such market operation, the restriction is unconstitutional.
